beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:setting the scene, wonder]At Marib, in Yemen, stand the ruins of a ^dam five hundred and eighty metres ^long: longer than five football pitches, end to ^end. [act:painting it, gently]It fed two ^gardens, one on ^each side of a valley. [act:the drama, lower, slower]And a ^flood that broke it ended a ^kingdom.

[d:tension][act:respectful, measured]The Quran recounts ^exactly this: the people of ^Saba, two gardens on the right and on the ^left, and the flood of the ^dam. [act:respectful, storytelling]The Bible and the Quran also tell of a queen of this land who visited King ^Solomon, whom the Quran calls ^Sulayman. [act:the open question, curious][tune:rise]What can the ^ground tell us about her journey?

[d:calm][act:confident, plain]Saba was ^real. [act:explaining, light]Sheba is simply the Bible's form of the same ^name. [act:warm, descriptive]A kingdom of ^incense, the fragrant resin burned in temples, rich enough that Assyrian kings logged its ^tribute. [go:3|0][p:0.93][act:quiet wonder, the scale]Its dam watered about a hundred square ^kilometres of fields, a square ten kilometres on each ^side, for more than a ^thousand years.

[d:build][act:sober, explaining]The dam was breached and repaired more than ^once. [act:sober, a little heavier]When it finally ^failed, in the sixth century CE, the water stopped, and the oases ^died. [act:respectful, quietly noting it]Just as the Quran ^recounts.

[d:build][act:turning a page, brisk]Now the ^visit. [act:precise, factual]The people of Saba wrote on stone, and their inscriptions begin around {750|seven fifty} BCE. [sfx:shimmer][act:the gap, slower]About two ^centuries after the time tradition gives to Solomon. [act:plain, even]They are full of kings, gods, dams and ^tribute. [act:plain, quiet, even]^None of them names a queen.

[d:build][act:sober, fair]Early Saba is ^barely excavated: its oldest layers lie deep, under everything that came after. [act:sober, plain]And since {2015|twenty fifteen}, war has ^stopped the digging. [d:aside][act:gentle, thoughtful, lighter]The queen, as the scriptures remember her, would have ruled ^before her country began to write things down.

[d:reveal][act:counting them off, confident]So the ground confirms the ^kingdom, the ^gardens, the ^dam, and the ^flood. [sfx:hit][act:quieter, precise]On the visit, it is ^silent. [p:0.93][act:calm, principled, firm]And silence in ^unexcavated ground is ^not a verdict: it is a page in a book nobody has ^opened yet.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, calm authority][tune:rise]Saba and its ^dam? [act:the verdict, confident][tune:fall]^*Established*. [act:gentler, open][tune:rise]The queen's ^journey, in the ground? [act:level-headed, respectful][tune:fall]Awaiting ^discovery.

[d:tension][p:0.93][act:respectful, sincere]We weigh only the ^ground, never the ^scriptures. [act:quiet wonder, inviting]Her traces ^may lie under the ^sand at Marib. [gap:0.45][act:the last word, soft and plain][tune:fall]^Nobody has looked yet.
